messages.subject: Re: Odd results from gmodels:CrossTable
parts:
On Fri, Dec 28, 2012 at 9:41 AM, Bob <muen...@tennessee.edu> wrote:
> The cross-tabulations for each gender appear, but are not labeled as usual.
> They are followed by optional output that I didn't request (row & column
> proportions, etc.) and those tables ARE labeled by gender. Since by() does
> the same thing, I

Interesting. Without seeing mydata100, I don't know what to say. I
suspect some errors from CrossTable are being swallowed up and so you
get that extra output as a result of its effort to fix up the
problems.

I also wonder:

1. Does same happen with by() ? Recall dlaply() is a convenience and
output management replacement for by...

2. Did you check to see if your function works properly on the
individual pieces of the dataset? Suppose you manufacture the data
for subgroups individually. what happens if you take the first group
in isolation, for example

with( mydata100[mydata100$gender %in% levels(mydata100$gender)[1], ]),
CrossTable(q1, q4, chisq = TRUE, format = "SAS"))

Or suppose you manufacture the subsets explicitly yourself in a list,
and use lapply.

PJ

Hi PJ,

The semester started & I got sidetracked. Those are some good questions. I made a running example. Yes, it does the same thing with "by" as with "dlply". Testing on the groups one at a time works fine. Example below.

Thanks,
Bob

gender <- sample(c("Male","Female"), 100, replace = TRUE)
group  <- sample(c("A","B"), 100, replace = TRUE)
treatment  <- sample(c("A","B"), 100, replace = TRUE)
mydata <- data.frame(gender, group, treatment)
rm(gender, group, treatment)

my_CrossTable <- function(x) {
  with(x,
       CrossTable(group, treatment,

# On whole data set, it works fine
library("gmodels")
my_CrossTable(mydata)

# On a subset it works fine
females <- mydata$gender == "Female"
my_CrossTable(mydata[females, ])

# Applied by group, it doesn't label the genders
# for the crosstabs. It also supplies way more
# output than it does when not applied by group!
# All the extra output IS labeled by gender.
dlply(mydata, .(gender), my_CrossTable)

# by does the same thing as dlply
by(mydata, mydata["gender"], my_CrossTable)
